hypotheses.statement: The checkout API 5xx spike was caused by the payments gateway certificate expiring at 09:11:40Z, which caused TLS handshake failures starting at 09:11:47Z
The release 2026.5.14-a was not the root cause of the incident, as it contained no changes to the checkout submit code path and the incident began after certificate expiration
The rollback to 2026.5.13-c did not cause the recovery, as the 5xx ratio had already returned to normal six minutes before the rollback completed
The incident response incorrectly attributed the problem to the release, leading to an unnecessary rollback

observed_facts.statement: Release 2026.5.14-a deployed at 09:09:52Z contained copy edits to email templates and a CSV export library dependency bump
No code path in release 2026.5.14-a is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit
Payments connector TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443 began at 09:11:47Z with error 'certificate verify failed: certificate has expired'
POST /v2/checkout/submit returned 502 upstream_unavailable after payments connector exhausted 3 retries
The 5xx ratio for POST /v2/checkout/submit was 0.184 against an objective of 0.005
p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose to 10400ms, which matches the configured client timeout
A sampled trace shows payments.authorize span timing out after 10388ms with no upstream response recorded
No span in the sampled trace entered the email template or CSV export code paths
Payments connector TLS handshakes succeeded again at 09:57:55Z
The payments-gateway leaf certificate expired at 09:11:40Z and was rotated at 09:57:50Z
The 5xx ratio had already returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before the rollback completed

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or runbook identifying certificate ownership and renewal process
open_questions.question: Who owns the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal certificate?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Incident response documentation or process records explaining impact assessment
open_questions.question: Why was no customer-impact estimate recorded during the incident?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Additional incident response communication or post-incident analysis
open_questions.question: Why did the resolution note only state 'rolled back and recovered' when evidence shows recovery preceded the rollback?

summary: Checkout API experienced a 5xx spike from 09:12:03Z to 09:58:10Z due to TLS handshake failures caused by an expired payments gateway certificate. The incident began 7 seconds after certificate expiration at 09:11:40Z and resolved after certificate rotation at 09:57:50Z. A coincidental release deployed 2 minutes before the incident was incorrectly attributed as the cause, leading to an unnecessary rollback after recovery had already occurred.

timeline.statement: payments connector TLS handshake failures begin due to expired certificate
checkout submit endpoint returns 502 upstream_unavailable after payments connector retries exhausted
alert fires: checkout-api error ratio above objective (5xx ratio 0.184)
alert fires: checkout-api latency objective burn (p99 latency rose to 10400ms)
incident ticket INC-7742 opened for checkout submit failures
responder attributes incident to the recent release
sampled trace shows payments.authorize span timing out after 10388ms
responder disputes release attribution, points to payments gateway certificate
payments connector TLS handshakes succeed again, error rate returns to baseline
payments-gateway team reports certificate expired at 09:11:40Z, rotated at 09:57:50Z
incident ticket marked resolved with note 'rolled back and recovered'
